story.intro: Companions of Grace International was born in 2019 through prayer and discernment among like-minded individuals carrying a shared conviction for Kingdom engagement and faithful Christian witness in the health fields of the world.

beliefs.heroSubtitle: Essential convictions that underlie our mission and purpose
beliefs.intro: We subscribe to the central beliefs of the historic church.

items.title: God
items.content: We believe there is one true God, eternally existing in three persons – Father, Son, and Holy Spirit- who we worship and glorify.

items.title: Jesus Christ
items.content: We believe in Jesus Christ, The Son of God, the Living Word (Logos), born of the virgin Mary, fully God and fully human - our Savior and Lord.

items.title: The Holy Spirit
items.content: We believe in the Holy Spirit – The Third Person of the Godhead, the giver of life, who glorifies Christ, convicts the world of sin, and accomplishes God's saving work in those who repent and believe — transforming and empowering them for witness and service through His gifts.

items.title: The Bible
items.content: We believe the Bible is the inspired, inerrant, and authoritative Word of God, forming the foundation of our faith, life, and mission.

items.title: The Universal Church
items.content: We believe in the Universal Church, for whom Christ is coming again, and with whom we seek to collaborate and partner in discipling and envisioning healthcare workers for missional healthcare

items.title: The Image of God
items.content: We believe in the Imago Dei that all people are created in God's image, yet fallen and under the power of sin and death and cannot belong to the Kingdom of God except through the new birth in Christ Jesus. Justification is by grace through faith in Christ alone.

items.title: The Kingdom of God
items.content: We believe the Kingdom of God is His sovereign reign over creation, revealed and redeemed in Christ Jesus through His sinless life, atoning death, bodily resurrection, Heavenly ascension.

items.title: Redemption
items.content: We believe His redemptive work is restorative, reconciling, and life-giving, renewing all things toward God’s purposes and bringing justice, peace, and flourishing to creation.

items.title: The Return of Christ
items.content: We believe the Kingdom will be consummated at the return of Christ Jesus. Until then, we are called to follow Jesus and join Him in building His Kingdom.

items.title: Our Calling in Healthcare
items.content: We believe, the calling in healthcare, is lived out through faithful witness, missional engagement and compassionate care.

board.heroSubtitle: Leaders committed to equipping healthcare professionals for Kingdom engagement

members.name: Abraham Thomas
members.title: Chairman
members.bio: With over three decades of experience in healthcare and church leadership, Abe serves as Chairman of the COGI Board. Based in New Jersey, he is a practicing pediatrician, President of the U.S. Chapter of Helping Hands for Hospitals, and an Elder at The Life Christian Church in West Orange. He and his wife, Ruby, have two sons, Ashish and Vivek; Vivek is married to Savannah, and they have a daughter, Georgia.

members.name: Mathew George Mulavelil
members.title: CEO & President
members.bio: Mathew George Mulavelil has devoted much of his career to healthcare mission, leadership, and formation. He spent two decades with the Emmanuel Hospital Association (EHA), based at Duncan Hospital, where he and his wife, Latha Mathew, pioneered its dental missions, establishing 14 dental units across the network, including the first at Duncan Hospital. He later served as Managing Director of Duncan Hospital. He then spent seven years with the Evangelical Medical Fellowship of India (EMFI), leading its Missions Department, where he developed mission training initiatives and strengthened its graduate ministry. As CEO and President of COGI, he continues to equip and mentor healthcare professionals for Kingdom engagement. He and Latha have a daughter, Rachel.

members.name: Charles Faust
members.title: Treasurer
members.bio: Chuck is a retired business executive who brings extensive global leadership experience from senior operating and financial roles with multinational companies headquartered in the United States, Japan, and Hong Kong. As COGI’s Treasurer and a close advisor to the CEO, he provides leadership in the development and oversight of the organization’s financial and administrative systems. He also contributes to COGI’s curriculum, particularly the Care for the Caregiver program, and assists with editing training resources. Chuck serves as an Elder in his local church. He and his wife, Mary, have been married for 40 years and live near Boise, Idaho, where they enjoy time with their three children and six grandchildren.

members.name: Sunil Abraham
members.title: Board Member
members.bio: Sunil Abraham is a practising Family Physician based in Rockhampton, Queensland, Australia. He previously served as Professor and Head of the Department of Family Medicine at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, India, becoming India’s first Professor of Family Medicine. Known for his wisdom, warmth, and thoughtful approach, he is deeply committed to serving God through healthcare, with a particular passion for discipleship and mentoring. He is also actively involved in ministry among the homeless through his church and community organizations. He is married to Mary, an ENT surgeon, and they have two daughters, Joanna and Erica.

members.name: Enoch Osafo
members.title: Board Member
members.bio: Mr. Enoch Osafo is a Lay Preacher in the Methodist Church Ghana, a registered Pharmacist with a Master’s in Public Health and an LLB. He is deeply committed to discipleship, initiatives of compassion, and the integration of faith and work. As former Health Director of the Methodist Church Ghana and Acting Director of Methodist Development and Relief Services, he helped strengthen the Church’s health and humanitarian ministries. His commitment to equipping healthcare professionals for mission led to the formation of the Annual Methodist Health Professionals Conference and Methodist Health Students in Mission. He has also engaged with US-based 501(c) organizations and the World Bank, strengthening systems that promote health and human dignity. He and his wife, Dr. Charlotte Osafo, a nephrologist and pioneer in kidney transplantation in Ghana, have four children—Sally, Benny, Lisbeth, and Lizette.

members.name: Molly Thomas
members.title: Board Member
members.bio: Molly is a dermatologist with over two decades of experience in mission healthcare, having served as a Consultant and Head of the Department at two mission hospitals in rural India before relocating to the United Kingdom. She remains deeply committed to nurturing Kingdom-minded healthcare professionals and strengthening healthcare mission initiatives. She and her husband, Viju John, a pediatric surgeon, have three children.

/programs.title: Discover the Kingdom of God
/programs.summary: Formational studies that reshape how you see, serve, and shape healthcare.
/programs.description: The Kingdom of God Program is a progressive formational journey that helps you align your life, calling, and service with God’s grand narrative.

experiences.title: Kingdom of God Seminar
experiences.description: A focused one-day or two-session formation experience introducing the biblical narrative of the Kingdom of God and its implications for life, calling, and healthcare praxis

experiences.title: Discovery Series
experiences.description: A three-series small group study exploring Jesus’ teachings on the Kingdom of God, integral health and healing, and compassionate care.

/programs.body: The Kingdom of God Program is a progressive formational journey that helps you align your life, calling, and service with God’s grand narrative.

/programs.title: Missional Healthcare Courses
/programs.summary: Missional trainings that shape you for Kingdom engagement.
/programs.description: The Missional Training Program helps healthcare students and professionals discern their place within God’s mission in the world. Grounded in Scripture, it invites you to see healthcare as missional.

experiences.description: An immersive internship that places healthcare students in real-world missional settings, with mentorship and community engagement.

experiences.title: Missional Health Course
experiences.description: A five-day residential training program that invites you to see your life and healthcare calling within the bigger picture of God’s mission in the world.

/programs.body: The Missional Training Program helps healthcare students and professionals discern their place within God’s mission in the world. Grounded in Scripture, it invites you to see healthcare as missional.

/programs.title: Care for the Caregiver
/programs.summary: Trainings and workshops that equip you to navigate the emotional, relational, and vocational challenges of caregiving.
/programs.description: Caregivers need care too. Those who devote themselves to caring for others often find it difficult to receive care themselves. The demands of caregiving can take a toll on emotional, relational, and personal well-being.

experiences.title: Eight-module journey
experiences.description: Develop Christ-centered resilience and relational wisdom to navigate life at work, at home, and in your community, caring for yourself and other caregivers.

/programs.summary: Seminars and programs envisioning church leaders and healthcare professionals for collaborative, missional engagement.
/programs.description: Equipping church leaders and healthcare workers to embrace healthcare as a vital expression of God’s redemptive work in the world.

experiences.title: HEAL Seminars
experiences.description: An eight-hour seminar helping church leaders rediscover healthcare as an integral expression of the Church’s mission.

experiences.title: HEAL Week
experiences.description: An annual church initiative celebrating and commissioning healthcare professionals. Get in touch to learn about this initiative as it develops.

/testimonials.author: Stella Osorio
/testimonials.quote: The Care for the Caregiver (C4C) Program helps create a safe space for reflection, emotional renewal, and spiritual strengthening. Through practical sessions on listening, communication, caring for the grieving, resilience, and Christ-centered caregiving, it equips us with valuable tools to care for ourselves and others more effectively. A deeply enriching and transformative experience that affirms the vital importance of caring for caregivers.

/testimonials.author: Abhilash Pappala
/testimonials.quote: Kingdom of God studies have transformed the way I understand and live my faith. They led me to genuine repentance and a deeper understanding of God’s grace and Kingdom purpose. Seeing life through a Kingdom lens has reshaped my attitudes, relationships, decisions, and stewardship, bringing greater clarity, purpose, and joy to everyday life.

/testimonials.author: Blessena
/testimonials.quote: Kingdom of God studies are highly interactive and practical, helping translate biblical teaching into everyday Kingdom living. They move beyond theory, guiding participants toward intentional steps shaped by God’s reign. The “I WILL” statements provide a simple framework for reflection and accountability, helping participants recognize and sustain their growth toward a Kingdom-centered lifestyle.
